[ Scoping ] · For chains

Eight steps. One ordering constraint.

What you do, and what you have when it is done.

You needA chain you control
You needA sequencer you run
You needA verifier you operate
You needAn L1 gas budget
#What you doWhat you have after
01 Deploy the Rollup managerinitialize(owner, threshold, proofSystems[], vkeys[]) A manager that can register, with your verifier set
02 Register on L1registerRollup(contract, initialRoot) A rollupId, assigned by the registry
03 Freeze your L2 genesis After 02The predeploy takes the rollupId at construction A chain that can carry cross-chain work, or a hard fork
04 Run the stackSequencer with a Sync block, composer, proof signer, deriver Batches posted and proven on L1
05 Open the frontsL1 and L2 ingress, plus your RPC Calls can land end to end
06 Mint proxiesOne per contract you want reachable Contracts other chains can call
07 Fund and monitorDeposits, inbound inventory, composer health A live integration
08 Prove itRun the conformance kit (planned) and publish the result A public conformance run

Why 02 precedes 03. The registry assigns your rollupId in the same transaction that notifies your manager, and the L2 predeploy needs that number at construction. You must land an L1 transaction before you can pin your L2 genesis. On a live chain, that means a hard fork after a counter you do not control.

Source: EEZ.sol and Rollup.sol at 143d87e. Conformance kit · Planned Addresses →
01

Still open

What this page cannot answer yet.
Canonical registry or your own?The only published deploy path deploys EEZ itself, while the mainnet registry has already issued six IDs. The shared model is implied, not stated.
Who runs composer and signer?Assumed to be the joining chain. If EEZ core operates them, that is a service commitment.
Is there a post-genesis path?Everything here assumes register-then-fork. Whether a live chain can join without a genesis change is settled on the scoping call.

Bring your stack to the call

Execution client, sequencer, genesis or live. We map it onto these eight before the call, not during it.
